source_text.body:
Send Sentry bugs to Copilot as GitHub issues for fixing
Author turned about 15 Sentry bugs into issues assigned to Copilot, which solved about 60% unaided; it was confidently wrong on failing Vitest tests.
·
Nov 10, 2025
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
Harrison clicked the button in Sentry that creates a GitHub issue for about 15 of his noisier bugs. He then assigned each issue to Copilot in GitHub, with no IDE involved. He suggests adding the Sentry MCP server to the repository for better context. He stepped in only where Copilot needed steering.
How it went
Copilot solved about 60% with no steering. A couple of fixes were bad enough that he closed them, and the rest needed one or two prompts. On failing Vitest tests in CI it was confidently wrong.
Worth knowing
Copilot used the .nvmrc Node version but his CI didn't, so its single-threaded Vitest change passed in its own run and made things worse. Rate limits and rebase conflicts also got in the way.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
Take the open Sentry errors for [project] that look fixable, and create a GitHub issue for each in [owner/repo] with the stack trace, frequency, and likely cause. Assign each issue to Copilot coding agent so it opens a draft PR. Do not merge anything; I will review each PR, and I want you to flag any PR where the tests are still failing.
Original source: https://harrisonmilbradt.com/blog/2025-11-10-an-honest-review-of-copilot-agents-hq
